on-pattern guide a request to dispatch an\\n  OpenAI-backed coding / review / research session loads.\\n\\nA bare CLI-dispatch phrase that names no executor (e.g. \\\"dispatch this to a CLI\\nexecutor\\\") names no mode, so it fires no intent and falls back to the hub default\\n(disambiguation) — the router does not silently default to `cli-opencode` on\\ngenuine ambiguity.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 2. MACHINE-READABLE ROUTER (replay / benchmark source)\\n\\nThe single machine-readable projection of the intent model above. The prose is\\nthe human-facing contract; this block is the byte-for-byte source the\\ndeterministic router-replay parses. Keep them in sync: when a map row changes\\nabove, update the matching `RESOURCE_MAP` entry here. Every `RESOURCE_MAP` path\\nresolves on disk and is registered in `leaf-manifest.json`, so each dual-reads to\\na canonical typed pair.\\n\\n```python\\n# No always-loaded preamble: CLI-dispatch routing loads only the selected mode's\\n# leaves so the hub default route stays minimal (disambiguation on no match).\\nDEFAULT_RESOURCE = []\\n\\nINTENT_SIGNALS = {\\n    \\\"OPENCODE\\\":    {\\\"weight\\\": 4, \\\"keywords\\\": [\\\"opencode\\\", \\\"opencode cli\\\", \\\"opencode run\\\", \\\"delegate to opencode\\\", \\\"cli-opencode\\\", \\\"parallel detached session\\\", \\\"full plugin runtime\\\", \\\"full plugin and memory stack\\\", \\\"spec kit runtime\\\", \\\"spec kit memory\\\", \\\"ablation suite\\\", \\\"worker farm opencode\\\"]},\\n    \\\"CLAUDE_CODE\\\": {\\\"weight\\\": 4, \\\"keywords\\\": [\\\"claude code\\\", \\\"claude cli\\\", \\\"cli-claude-code\\\", \\\"anthropic cli\\\", \\\"anthropic cli second opinion\\\", \\\"delegate to claude\\\", \\\"extended thinking\\\", \\\"deep reasoning handoff\\\", \\\"deeply-reasoned opinion\\\", \\\"structured claude code output\\\", \\\"claude code review\\\"]},\\n    \\\"CODEX\\\":       {\\\"weight\\\": 4, \\\"keywords\\\": [\\\"codex\\\", \\\"codex cli\\\", \\\"codex exec\\\", \\\"cli-codex\\\", \\\"openai cli second opinion\\\", \\\"delegate to codex\\\", \\\"openai coding agent\\\", \\\"codex web search\\\", \\\"codex diff review\\\", \\\"codex sandbox\\\", \\\"gpt codex dispatch\\\"]},\\n}\\n\\nRESOURCE_MAP = {\\n    \\\"OPENCODE\\\": [\\n        \\\"cli-opencode/references/cli-reference.md\\\",\\n        \\\"cli-opencode/references/integration-patterns.md\\\"\\n    ],\\n    \\\"CLAUDE_CODE\\\": [\\n        \\\"cli-claude-code/references/cli-reference.md\\\",\\n        \\\"cli-claude-code/references/integration-patterns.md\\\"\\n    ],\\n    \\\"CODEX\\\": [\\n        \\\"cli-codex/references/cli-reference.md\\\",\\n        \\\"cli-codex/references/integration-patterns.md\\\"\\n    ],\\n}\\n```\\n\\n## 3. How to read this\\n\\n- One dominant executor intent routes to one mode's leaf set.\\n- Two near-tied intents (within the ambiguity delta) route to both leaf sets; the\\n  union is deduped by canonical pair and capped at the selected-map union limit —\\n  the `orderedBundle` outcome `hub-router.json` declares.\\n- Each mode's leaves are its own CLI command reference plus its integration-pattern\\n  guide; the deeper per-mode references (tool catalogs, permission matrices,\\n  self-invocation guards) load on demand inside the packet, not on the first slice.\\n- No keyword match is the hub's `defer` fallback: confirm the target executor\\n  (`cli-opencode`, `cli-claude-code`, or `cli-codex`) before loading anything.\\n\\nexec\\n/bin/zsh -lc \\\"sed -n '320,700p' .opencode/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/SKILL.md\\\" in .worktrees/0089-sk-doc-default-routing-cutover\\n succeeded in 0ms:\\n\\n### Task Completion\\n\\n- OpenCode CLI invoked with the correct subcommand, flags, model, agent, variant, format, and dir.\\n- Self-invocation guard checked before dispatch — refused when appropriate.\\n- Use case (1 / 2 / 3) classified explicitly before invocation.\\n- JSON event stream captured, parsed incrementally, validated, integrated.\\n- No security vulnerabilities introduced from generated code.\\n- `--share` URLs opt-in with operator confirmation per CHK-033.\\n- Background dispatches in `while read` loops include `</dev/null` redirect.\\n- Memory Handback extracted and saved through `generate-context.js` when applicable.\\n\\n### Skill Quality\\n\\n- All numbered sections present and correctly ordered.\\n- Smart routing covers all intent signals with UNKNOWN_FALLBACK.\\n- Reference files provide deep-dive content without duplication.\\n- Self-invocation guard pseudocode reproduced in Section 2 mirrors ADR-001.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 7. INTEGRATION POINTS\\n\\n### Framework Integration\\n\\nThis skill operates within the behavioral framework defined in [AGENTS.md](../../../../AGENTS.md).\\n\\nKey integrations:\\n- **Gate 2**: Skill routing via the Skill Advisor Hook (or `skill_advisor.py` fallback)\\n- **Tool Routing**: Per AGENTS.md Section 6 decision tree\\n- **Memory**: Context preserved via Spec Kit Memory MCP (`generate-context.js`)\\n- **Validation**: `bash .opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/spec/validate.sh` for spec-folder workflows\\n\\n**Tool roles**: Bash dispatches the CLI; Read/Glob/Grep validate output and probe `~/.opencode/state/` for session locks.\\n\\nexec\\n/bin/zsh -lc \\\"sed -n '125,220p' .opencode/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/SKILL.md; sed -n '220,319p' .opencode/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/SKILL.md\\\" in .worktrees/0089-sk-doc-default-routing-cutover\\n succeeded in 0ms:\\n\\nUNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = [\\n    \\\"Is the user asking about OpenCode CLI specifically?\\\",\\n    \\\"Does the task need the project's full plugin / skill / MCP runtime?\\\",\\n    \\\"Is a parallel detached session what they want?\\\",\\n    \\\"Is a non-Anthropic CLI handing back to OpenCode for a spec-kit workflow?\\\",\\n]\\n```\\n\\n**Call sequence** (using shared helpers from `shared-smart-router.md`):\\n\\n1. `discover_markdown_resources()` — recursively enumerate current `.md` files under existing `references/` and `assets/` folders at routing time.\\n2. `_guard_in_skill()` + `load_if_available()` — sandbox paths to this skill, reject non-markdown loads, skip missing files, and suppress duplicates.\\n3. `score_intents(task)` and `select_intents(scores, ambiguity_delta=1.0)` — preserve provider-specific weighted intent scoring and top-2 ambiguity handling.\\n4. ALWAYS-load `LOADING_LEVELS[\\\"ALWAYS\\\"]`, then return `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK` with `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST` when max score is 0.\\n5. CONDITIONAL-load existing `RESOURCE_MAP[intent]` entries via `load_if_available()`, ON_DEMAND-load keyword matches, and return a notice when no intent-specific knowledge base is available beyond always-load resources.\\n\\nThe `route_opencode_resources(task)` function body lives in [`shared-smart-router.md`](../../system-spec-kit/references/cli/shared-smart-router.md) — substitute `<PROVIDER>` = `opencode`.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 3. HOW IT WORKS\\n\\n### Prerequisites\\n\\n```bash\\n# Verify installation (cli-opencode v1.0.0 is pinned to opencode v1.3.17)\\nopencode --version | grep -q '^1\\\\.' || echo \\\"Not installed or version drift. See references/cli-reference.md §9.\\\"\\n\\n# Self-invocation guard\\nenv | grep -q '^OPENCODE_' && echo \\\"ERROR: Already inside OpenCode session\\\"\\n\\n# Authentication — providers configured via opencode providers (alias auth)\\nopencode providers\\n```\\n\\n**Authentication options**: `opencode providers login <provider>` (and `opencode auth login` for subscription plans). Full per-provider login shapes and the configured-provider list: `references/cli-reference.md` §4.\\n\\n### Provider Auth Pre-Flight (Smart Fallback)\\n\\n**MANDATORY before any first dispatch in a session.** The default provider may not be logged in — silently failing with `provider/model not found` or `401 Unauthorized` mid-dispatch wastes a round-trip. Run the pre-flight once per session, cache the result, and re-run only on an auth failure.\\n\\nThe one-shot pre-flight bash, the per-provider decision trees, the user-facing prompt templates for missing providers, and the error-recovery contract live in [`references/cli-reference.md`](./references/cli-reference.md) §4 — do not duplicate them here. Never substitute a model the user didn't approve; ASK when the default is unavailable.\\n\\n### Default Invocation (Skill Default)\\n\\n**Default model + variant + format + dir**: `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` · `--variant high` · `--format json` · `--dir <repo-root>` (pinned to avoid CWD ambiguity). Direct DeepSeek is the default provider — elevated reasoning at low cost for routine dispatches.\\n\\nUse `opencode run --model deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro --variant high --format json --dir <repo-root> \\\"<prompt>\\\"`.\\n\\n> **The `--agent` flag (read this):** Do NOT pass `--agent` on a top-level `opencode run` — current opencode treats named agents like `general` as **subagents** and rejects them at the top level, so `--agent general` fails outright. The default agent runs when `--agent` is omitted, which is correct for almost every dispatch. **To target a specific agent profile, describe the role in the prompt body instead** (e.g. open with \\\"Act as a code-review agent: …\\\"); only pass `--agent <name>` after confirming acceptance via `opencode run --help` on the installed version.\\n\\nHonor explicit user model, port, and handback phrasing verbatim; otherwise use the default invocation above.\\n\\n### Core Invocation Pattern\\n\\nCore flags: `--model`, `--agent`, `--variant`, `--format json`, `--dir`, continuation/session/fork flags, `--share` and `--port` for detached sessions, `--file`, `--thinking`, `--pure`, and log flags.\\n\\n> **Non-interactive invocation stdin**: always append `</dev/null` to any non-interactive `opencode run` invocation — without it, opencode can inherit parent-terminal stdin and hang. See `references/integration-patterns.md` §6.\\n\\n> **Registered command dispatch (`--command`)**: slash-command text inside a `run` message is NOT expanded — `opencode run \\\"/memory:search query\\\"` delivers the slash text as raw prose. Execute a registered command via `opencode run --command <family>/<name> [flags] \\\"<args>\\\"` (becomes `$ARGUMENTS`; e.g. `memory/search` for `/memory:search`). Full semantics: `references/cli-reference.md` §4.\\n\\n### Model Selection\\n\\nRun `opencode providers list` to confirm credentials and `opencode models <provider>` for live choices. Default: `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro --variant high` (direct DeepSeek API). Alternates (all omit `--agent`): MiniMax Token Plan/Direct API `MiniMax-M3`, Xiaomi Token Plan/Direct API `mimo-v2.5-pro` (+ low-latency `-ultraspeed`), Kimi For Coding `k2p7` (256k, subscription), Z.AI GLM Coding Plan `glm-5.2` (1M, subscription), and the OpenAI GPT-5.6 catalog (`gpt-5.6-sol` flagship default; bare/Sol/Terra/Luna x base/Fast/Pro, `--variant` up to `xhigh`). Full model table, per-provider `--variant` mapping, and model-specific operational caveats: `references/cli-reference.md` §5.\\n\\nShared small-model facts, context defaults, quota pools, and fallback targets live in `../../sk-prompt/prompt-models/assets/model-profiles.json`.\\n\\n### OpenCode Agent Delegation\\n\\nThe calling AI is the conductor. OpenCode distinguishes **primary agents** (directly invokable via `--agent <slug>`) from **subagents** (dispatched as Task-tool subagents from a primary).\\n\\n#### Primary agents — directly invokable via `--agent`\\n\\nOpenCode defines `general`, `plan`, and `orchestrate` as primary agents. **Never pass `--agent general`** — it is rejected at the top level; the default agent (used when `--agent` is omitted) already covers that case. Pin `--agent plan|orchestrate` only when the task needs that profile AND `opencode run --help` confirms top-level acceptance; otherwise state the role in the prompt body.\\n\\n#### Subagents — dispatched as Task subagents from a primary\\n\\nThese live at `.opencode/agents/<slug>.md` with `mode: subagent` and are NOT directly invokable via `opencode run --agent`. Three dispatch surfaces are legal under the single-hop NDP contract:\\n\\n1. **Generic subagents** (`context`, `review`, `write`, `debug`) — dispatched by `orchestrate` via the Task tool. Route through `--agent orchestrate` and let it dispatch the relevant subagent.\\n2. **`ai-council`** — dispatched via `/deep:ai-council` or `orchestrate`'s registry-backed Task-dispatch. Direct `--agent ai-council` is rejected at the top level (`mode: subagent`).\\n3. **Command-owned loop executors** (`deep-research`, `deep-review`, `deep-improvement`, `prompt-improver`) — LOOP-OWNED by their parent commands (`/deep:research`, `/deep:review`, `/deep:agent-improvement`, `/prompt`), which own iteration state, convergence detection, and continuity. Never dispatch these directly via raw `--agent <slug>`. `orchestrate` is an authorized **caller/coordinator only** — it may perform exactly one bounded hand-off dispatch to the resolved leaf, but MUST NOT re-implement the loop.\\n\\nSee [agent-delegation.md](./references/agent-delegation.md) for the complete agent roster and dispatch patterns.\\n\\n### Unique OpenCode Strengths\\n\\nFull project runtime loading, detached sessions, JSON event streams, agent routing, cross-repo/server dispatch, session continuation, and plugin-disable debugging.\\n\\n### Essential Commands\\n\\nDefault invocation for external runtime handback; `--share --port <N>` only for explicit detached sessions; `--agent orchestrate` for generic subagent routing; `--dir` for cross-repo dispatch.\\n\\n### Error Handling\\n\\n\\nInstall missing binaries, refuse ambiguous self-invocation, run provider pre-flight for model/auth errors, check version drift for unknown flags, force `--format json` for empty streams, add `</dev/null` for background loops, confirm `--share`, use `--pure` only for plugin crashes, inspect state logs for stuck sessions.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 4. RULES\\n\\n### ✅ ALWAYS\\n\\n1. Verify OpenCode CLI is installed before first invocation; confirm version baseline against v1.3.17 (drift handling per `references/cli-reference.md` §9).\\n2. **Run the self-invocation guard before dispatch** (ADR-001): Layer 1 env-var lookup for any `OPENCODE_*`, Layer 2 process-ancestry probe for `opencode` parent, Layer 3 `~/.opencode/state/<id>/lock` probe. Trip on ANY positive — refuse unless prompt has explicit parallel-session keywords.\\n3. Pin model + variant + format + dir explicitly — **no `--agent`** (see the Default Invocation note: current opencode rejects a top-level `--agent general`; put any agent-profile request in the prompt body). Default: `--model deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro --variant high --format json --dir <repo-root>`. Honor user overrides verbatim (e.g. `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`, `minimax-coding-plan/MiniMax-M3`, `minimax/MiniMax-M3`, `xiaomi-token-plan-ams/mimo-v2.5-pro`, `xiaomi/mimo-v2.5-pro`, `xiaomi/mimo-v2.5-pro-ultraspeed`, `openai/gpt-5.6-sol-pro`).\\n4. Pass `--format json` unless the calling AI explicitly wants formatted output — JSON event stream is what external runtimes parse incrementally.\\n5. **Append `</dev/null` to every non-interactive `opencode run` invocation** that redirects stdout and/or stderr to files OR runs inside `while read` loops. opencode v1.14.39 reads stdin at startup before session creation; without explicit closed stdin, automation hangs forever at 0% CPU after the `+60s service=snapshot prune=7.days cleanup` log line. Position: AFTER the prompt positional argument, BEFORE the `> stdout 2> stderr` redirects. Foreground `| tail` happens to provide closed stdin (pipe stage upstream is empty) and accidentally bypasses the bug, but `> stdout.log 2> stderr.log` does not. The 9-character `</dev/null` redirect provides immediate EOF on stdin, unblocking the dispatch. **DO NOT auto-kill external operator-owned opencode sessions** when sweeping orphans between dispatches; exclude `opencode run` from pkill (per 2026-05-23 operator directive captured in memory `feedback_proactive_orphan_cleanup.md`). See `references/integration-patterns.md` §6 + memory `feedback_opencode_run_requires_dev_null_stdin.md` + CHANGELOG-2026-05-08-tool-name-regex-fix.md §Fix 4.\\n6. **Pass the spec folder to the dispatched session** in the prompt: if the calling AI has an active Gate-3 spec folder, include `Spec folder: <path> (pre-approved, skip Gate 3)`. If none, ASK the user before delegating — the dispatched session cannot answer Gate 3 interactively in non-interactive `run` mode.\\n7. **Prompt construction & model-craft (cli-* family precedence).** Compose every dispatch prompt via the 3-tier rule canonical in `../../sk-prompt/prompt-models/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md`:\\n   1. **Fast path (default).** Build from the local `assets/prompt-quality-card.md`, which delegates the framework table + CLEAR check to the canonical card.\\n   2. **Model override (mandatory for a profiled model).** If the target model has a profile at `../../sk-prompt/prompt-models/references/models/<id>.md`, that profile OVERRIDES the cross-model default. The **sk-prompt/prompt-models** hub owns per-model prompt-craft (framework + scaffold + gotchas, mirroring `sk-prompt/prompt-models/assets/model-profiles.json` `recommended_frameworks`); consult it before composing for any small model.\\n   3. **Deep path (escalation).** Dispatch `@prompt-improver` via the Task tool (never load full `sk-prompt` inline) when any canonical **Tier 3** trigger applies — the trigger list lives in `../../sk-prompt/prompt-models/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` under \\\"Tier 3 — Deep path\\\"; do not re-enumerate it here.\\n8. Validate dispatched session output: parse JSON events incrementally (tool calls, partial messages, final summary), run syntax checks if code generated, and cross-reference against project standards via `sk-code` surface detection plus its code-review mode when findings-first review is requested (see ALWAYS rule 12).\\n9. Capture stderr (`2>&1`) to catch tool errors and warnings.\\n10. Classify the use case (1 / 2 / 3) before dispatching — the smart router refuses dispatches that do not map to one of the three.\\n11. **Run the Provider Auth Pre-Flight once per session** (see §3 Provider Auth Pre-Flight). Cache the configured-providers list. If the default `deepseek` is missing, ASK the user — never silently substitute the model. If a later dispatch returns an auth error, invalidate the cache and rerun the pre-flight before retrying.\\n12. **Code Standards Loading (surface-aware contract)** — When dispatching for code review or code generation, instruct the dispatched session to: (1) load `sk-code`; (2) let `sk-code` emit a surface tag matching the detected stack from markers and target files; (3) load the selected surface resources and run its verification commands; (4) load `sk-code`'s code-review mode only for formal findings-first review output. Fallback: if the surface cannot be determined confidently, ask for the runtime surface and verification command set. NEVER hardcode obsolete sibling code skills in dispatch prompts.\\n13. **Design Standards Loading (surface-aware contract)** — When dispatching for design or UI work, instruct the dispatched session to: (1) load `sk-design` (the hub); (2) let the hub resolve a `workflowMode` through `mode-registry.json` (interface / foundations / motion / audit / md-generator / design-mcp-open-design); (3) load the selected mode packet, set the design register, and run that mode's design verification; (4) if the work feeds Open Design, carry the `design-mcp-open-design` pairing (a nested transport packet of the hub) — the transport never decides taste. Fallback: if the design mode cannot be determined confidently, ask for the surface and design intent. NEVER treat `mcp-figma` or `design-mcp-open-design` as the taste authority, or hardcode obsolete flat design skills in dispatch prompts.\\n14. **Pass the design dispatch manifest to the dispatched session** — when dispatching design or UI work, inline a `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST v1` block in the prompt (the child cannot resolve skill paths, so the manifest travels in the payload, not by reference): `skDesignLoaded` true, `register` resolved to `Brand` or `Product` (never `unknown`), registry-valid `workflowModes`, `dials`, `loadedFiles`, and `proofDemandBack`. The child returns the demanded proof; the parent reconciles it on the return path.\\n15. **Destructive-scope-violation prevention (RM-8) for deep-loop dispatches** — The structured permissions-matrix gate (`permissions-gate.ts`; schema and design in `references/permissions-matrix.md`) is built and unit-tested but has ZERO production callers today — no `opencode run` dispatch path invokes it, so a loaded `--permissions-matrix <path>` config or recipe field is NOT currently enforced and does NOT bypass anything. # Hermes Agent CLI Orchestrator - Cross-AI Task Delegation

> **CRITICAL — SELF-INVOCATION PROHIBITED**
>
> This skill dispatches to the Hermes Agent binary (`hermes`). If the agent currently reading this
> skill is itself running inside Hermes (detection signals in [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md) §3), the skill
> MUST refuse to load and return the documented error instead of generating any `hermes` invocation.
> Hermes has in-process delegation of its own (`delegate_task`), so a Hermes session hands work out
> through that, never by re-dispatching this CLI.

Orchestrate Hermes Agent (Nous Research's open-source, Python-based agent CLI) for quiet oneshot
coding dispatch, cross-AI validation, and model routing through the operator's LLM Gateway
provider. The evidence base is the research synthesis and the live contract pin:
[research synthesis](../../../specs/cli-external-orchestration/071-cli-hermes-creation/001-deep-research/research/research.md),
[contract pin](../../../specs/cli-external-orchestration/071-cli-hermes-creation/002-hermes-contract-pin/implementation-summary.md).
Claims marked **source-read, unconfirmed** come from the installed Hermes source (v0.21.1) and stay
unconfirmed until a live run records otherwise.

**Core principle**: use Hermes for what its surface offers, delegate research and review lineages to the shared
deep-loop runtime, validate the returned output, and keep the calling AI as conductor.

---

## 1. WHEN TO USE

### Activation Triggers

- **Headless Hermes dispatch**: the task explicitly names Hermes, Nous Research, or the Hermes agent.
- **Cross-AI validation**: an independent implementation attempt, review, or second opinion through a Hermes-hosted model.
- **LLM Gateway roster dispatch**: a task that wants `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash` or `glm-5.3-flash` through Hermes's tool loop rather than Pi's or OpenCode's.
- **Project skills and plugins**: a task that concerns Hermes's repo-local `.hermes/skills`, `.hermes/plugins`, or its skill and plugin commands.
- **Deep-loop fan-out**: a `/deep:research` or `/deep:review` lineage on `--executor=cli-hermes`.

14: # Hermes MCP Policy
15: 
16: Hermes hosts MCP servers, but only from the operator's configuration. This is a structural difference from every sibling runtime, which registers servers in a repo dotfolder.
17: 
18: ## 1. OVERVIEW
19: 
20: ### Purpose
21: 
22: MCP servers reach a Hermes session only from the operator's user-level configuration; this reference records that boundary, the one operator step, the deny-by-default posture and what a dispatch may assume.
23: 
24: ### When to Use
25: 
26: - Working out whether a server is reachable from a Hermes dispatch at all.
27: - Adding the repo's code-mode server as the operator.
28: - Locking a newly added server down to the tools one task needs.
29: 
30: ---
31: 
32: ## 2. WHERE MCP LIVES
33: 
34: - **Config source:** `mcp_servers:` is read from `~/.hermes/config.yaml` only (source-read: `hermes_cli/mcp_config.py`).
35: - **Server management:** `hermes mcp add|remove|list|test|configure` manage it.
36: - **Tool toggles:** `hermes tools list|disable|enable`, with `server:tool` notation.
37: - **Per-run off switch:** `--safe-mode` disables all MCP servers for a run.
38: - **Cold start:** the `chat` path waits for MCP cold start before its first tool snapshot, so a configured server adds startup latency to every dispatch.
39: 
40: ---
41: 
42: ## 3. THE OPERATOR STEP
43: 
44: To reach the repo's code-mode server from Hermes, the operator runs, once:
45: 
46: A dispatch never runs these.
47: 
48: ```bash
49: printf 'Y\n' | hermes mcp add code_mode --command node --env UTCP_CONFIG_FILE=.utcp_config.json --args .skilled/bin/mcp-code-mode-launcher.cjs
50: hermes mcp list
51: ```
52: 
53: Observed 2026-09-14:
54: 
55: - `--args` must be the last option.
56: - The command connects and discovers seven tools.
57: - The "Enable all tools?" prompt needs an answer on stdin; a closed stdin cancels the add.
58: 
59: A session reaches the server only when its name appears in the `-t` list (`-t search,todo,code_mode`).
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: ## 4. DENY BY DEFAULT
64: 
65: After adding a server, disable every tool and enable the few a task needs:
66: 
67: ```bash
68: hermes tools disable code_mode
69: hermes tools enable code_mode:search_tools code_mode:call_tool_chain
70: ```
71: 
72: Pre-spawn security filters drop configurations shaped like exfiltration; OAuth device flow covers remote servers. `hermes mcp serve` (Hermes as an MCP server) has no consumer in this repo and is not part of this policy.
73: 
74: ---
75: 
76: ## 5. WHAT A DISPATCH MAY ASSUME
77: 
78: Nothing about MCP unless `hermes mcp list` shows the server. A prompt that needs a tool from a server checks the list first, and stops with a report if the server is absent. The packet's hard rule `mcp-config-operator-required` states this boundary.

15: # Hermes Agent Delegation Reference
16: 
17: This reference prevents a category error: Hermes profiles and `delegate_task` sub-agents are not persona surfaces for this repo's agents.
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: Records every route a repo persona can take into a Hermes dispatch, and the reason a profile or a `delegate_task` child cannot stand in for one.
24: 
25: ### When to Use
26: 
27: - Composing a dispatch that carries a resolved agent persona
28: - Deciding whether to preload `agent-<name>` or inline the persona
29: - Checking what a `delegate_task` child may and may not do
30: - Finding the prompt template for a nested `.skilled/commands` command
31: 
32: ### Core Principle
33: 
34: The repo's agents (`.skilled/agents/*.md`, the authored source) reach a Hermes dispatch only inside the prompt. Hermes has no flag that loads an agent file, its profiles are whole-home islands, and `delegate_task` children receive a goal and context, never an agent definition.
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. PERSONA ROUTES
39: 
40: | Route | Works | Use when |
41: |---|---|---|
42: | Inline the persona block at the top of the prompt, after the child-dispatch preamble | Yes | Default; the `cli-codex` and `cli-pi` precedent |
43: | Persona skill preloaded with `-s <name>` from `./.hermes/skills` | Yes, after the trust grant | Only if prompt size becomes a measured problem; needs the repo-local folder and the operator's trust |
44: | `hermes profile create` per agent | No | Profiles isolate homes and credentials, not personas |
45: | `hermes import-agent claude-code` | No | Imports `CLAUDE.md` into memories and copies skills into the user home; never imports agent files; bypasses trust and quarantine |
46: 
47: Resolve the persona from the calling runtime's agent directory (AGENTS.md §9), since Hermes has none of its own and its personas travel inlined in the prompt, and map each subtask to the right agent (code, review, design, deep-research, markdown). The canonical contract is `../../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` "Persona Injection".
48: 
49: ---
50: 
51: ## 3. COMMANDS
52: 
53: The repo's nested commands under `.skilled/commands/**` have no Hermes equivalent: Hermes has no workflow engine and its slash commands are its own. The cli-pi precedent applies: flatten each command into a prompt template under `.hermes/prompts/` and carry it with `--query-file`. A sync script generates those templates; a dispatch loads the template text into its prompt file.
54: 
55: ---
56: 
57: ## 4. PERSONA THROUGH THE REPO PLUGIN
58: 
59: `.hermes/agents/` links the shared runtime-neutral agent files, and `sync-skills-hermes.cjs` mirrors each as the preloadable skill `agent-<name>` because Hermes has no agent flag and caps a plugin prompt section at 4000 characters (a 22k persona in a section was skipped outright).
60: 
61: The native-shaped dispatch pairs:
62: 
63: - `-s agent-<name>`, the skill that carries the whole persona
64: - `HERMES_AGENT_PERSONA=<name>`, the name the plugin's persona section binds for the session
65: 
66: `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS=1` must be set for the plugin to load.
67: 
68: `--ignore-rules` is passed alongside `-s`: a live A/B under the flag showed the preload still reaching the model, so omitting it only bled SOUL.md, memories and session search into the leaf. Inline stays the fallback for a run without the plugin or the mirror.
69: 
70: ---
71: 
72: ## 5. SKILLS
73: 
74: With the repo trusted, Hermes loads the curated per-skill links under `.hermes/skills/<name>` and can preload one with `-s <name>` (observed 2026-09-14: `-s cli-hermes` quoted the packet's first hard rule). A dispatch that needs any other skill names it in the prompt by path, because only linked skills are visible to Hermes and the hub identity does not cross the link.
75: 
76: ---
77: 
78: ## 6. `delegate_task` AND THE DELEGATION BOUNDARY
79: 
80: Hermes's own sub-agents are spawned by the `delegation` toolset. A leaf lineage never carries that toolset: a sub-agent spawned inside a lineage runs outside the runner's containment and stack guards. For non-leaf use, the semantics of `delegation.subagent_auto_approve`, child timeouts and flag inheritance are open questions for the contract pin. Because Hermes has in-process delegation, `cli-hermes` is not exempt from the self-presence guards the way `cli-pi` is.
81: 
82: ---
83: 
84: ## 7. MCP AND HOOKS AS DELEGATION SURFACES
85: 
86: MCP servers are user-level ([mcp-policy.md](./mcp-policy.md)); the repo's guard cores reach a Hermes session through the project plugin ([hook-contract.md](./hook-contract.md)). Neither is a persona surface.

16: # Hermes CLI - Complete Command Reference
17: 
18: This reference records the Hermes contract as read from the installed source (v0.21.1, upstream `dc90a75a`, git install at `~/.hermes/hermes-agent`) and from live help output on 2026-09-14. Claims marked **source-read** await the contract pin; the one live observation is marked **observed**.
19: 
20: Sources: [research synthesis](../../../../specs/cli-external-orchestration/071-cli-hermes-creation/001-deep-research/research/research.md), [contract pin](../../../../specs/cli-external-orchestration/071-cli-hermes-creation/002-hermes-contract-pin/implementation-summary.md).
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Purpose
25: 
26: Be the single source a dispatcher checks before running Hermes, so every flag, exit code and approval rule a run depends on is looked up rather than remembered.
27: 
28: ### When to Use
29: 
30: - Composing or auditing a `hermes chat` dispatch command
31: - Looking up a flag, an exit code or an environment variable
32: - Deciding whether a run may write or must stay read-only
33: 
34: Hermes Agent is a Python agent CLI with a large tool surface (terminal, file, search, web, browser, vision, delegation, memory, skills, MCP) and a provider catalog of some forty providers. The binary is `hermes`; `hermes --version` prints the version, install method and install directory. Record the installed version at execution time.
35: 
36: Hermes has three headless forms, and only one is auditable:
37: 
38: | Form | Invocation | Stdout | Session id | Approvals |
39: |---|---|---|---|---|
40: | Quiet oneshot chat (**use this**) | `hermes chat -Q --oneshot -q "<prompt>"` or `--query-file <path>` | Final response only | `session_id: <id>` on stderr | Flagged actions blocked; `--yolo` lifts the gate |
41: | Non-TTY chat | `hermes chat -q "<prompt>"` with stdio not a TTY | Response plus banner and previews unless `-Q` | On stderr | Same as above |
42: | Top-level oneshot (**never for dispatch**) | `hermes -z "<prompt>"` | Final response only | None | Auto-approves everything and auto-accepts hooks |
43: 
44: ---
45: 
46: ## 2. FLAGS THAT MATTER FOR DISPATCH
47: 
48: | Flag | Effect | Standing |
49: |---|---|---|
50: | `-q, --query TEXT` | The prompt in argv; on a non-TTY it answers and exits | live help |
51: | `--query-file PATH` | Read the prompt from a file, `-` for stdin, nothing shell-interpreted; mutually exclusive with `-q` | live help |
52: | `--oneshot` | Answer and exit; implied on non-TTY stdio and by `-Q` | live help |
53: | `-Q, --quiet` | Suppress banner, spinner and tool previews; print only the final response and session info | live help |
54: | `-m, --model ID` | Model id for this run | live help |
55: | `--provider NAME` | Built-in provider or a user-defined name from `providers:` in `config.yaml`; the packet pins `llmgateway` | live help |
56: | `--reasoning LEVEL` | `none minimal low medium high xhigh max ultra`, the same set as the runtime's effort enum | live help |
57: | `-t, --toolsets LIST` | Comma-separated toolsets to enable; replaces the configured set | live help |
58: | `-s, --skills LIST` | Preload skills for the session | live help |
59: | `--yolo` | Auto-approve the tool calls Hermes flags as dangerous; ordinary writes need no flag (observed 2026-09-14) | live help |
60: | `--ignore-rules` | Skip `AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, `.cursorrules` and memory injection. Hermes's help text also claims it skips preloaded skills; a live A/B disproved that, so `-s` and this flag travel together | live help, preload clause **corrected by observation 2026-09-15** |
61: | `--ignore-user-config` | Ignore `~/.hermes/config.yaml`; `.env` credentials still load | live help |
62: | `--safe-mode` | Disable user config, rules, plugins and MCP servers | live help |
63: | `--max-turns N` | Turn cap for the run (Hermes default 500) | live help |
64: | `--run-budget SECONDS` | Wall-clock budget; the agent wraps up as it expires | live help |
65: | `--source tool` | Keep the run out of the operator's session lists | live help |
66: | `--in DIR` | Change into DIR before starting | live help |
67: | `--accept-hooks` | Auto-approve unseen shell hooks; never pass unless the operator declared hooks | live help |
68: | `--worktree` | Run in an isolated git worktree; **never pass from a dispatch** (writes `.git/worktrees/` inside the repo) | live help |
69: | `--pass-session-id` | Put the session id into the system prompt | live help |

15: # Hermes Hook Contract
16: 
17: Hermes has two hook surfaces. One is the operator's; one the repo can carry.
18: 
19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: Hermes keeps shell hooks in the operator's user-level config and reads a repo plugin from `.hermes/plugins/`. This reference records both surfaces and the plugin hook map that carries the repo's guard cores into a Hermes session.
24: 
25: ### When to Use
26: 
27: - Deciding whether a guard belongs in a shell hook or the project plugin.
28: - Checking which hook each repo guard core runs on.
29: - Validating the plugin after a guard core changes.
30: 
31: ---
32: 
33: ## 2. SHELL HOOKS (USER-LEVEL)
34: 
35: Shell-script hooks:
36: 
37: - **Declared:** under `hooks:` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`.
38: - **Gated:** by a per-command consent allowlist at `~/.hermes/shell-hooks-allowlist.json`.
39: - **Inspected:** with `hermes hooks list|test|doctor`.
40: - **Bypassed:** on a headless run by `--accept-hooks` or `HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS=1`; `hermes -z` sets it automatically.
41: 
42: The repo cannot declare these. None is configured on this machine (observed 2026-09-14: `hooks:` absent, `~/.hermes/hooks/` empty). A dispatch never passes `--accept-hooks` unless the operator declared hooks and asked for it.
43: 
44: ---
45: 
46: ## 3. PROJECT PLUGIN (REPO-CARRIABLE)
47: 
48: Native plugins load from `./.hermes/plugins/<name>/` when `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS` is set, and their hook list covers every guard core this repo runs (source-read: `hermes_cli/plugins.py`). The plugin at `.hermes/plugins/repo-guards/` re-implements nothing:
49: 
50: - Each hook shells out to the existing `.mjs` or `.sh` core under `.skilled/hooks/`.
51: - It maps the core's result to Hermes's block-or-continue contract.
52: - It fails open on a core error, as the `.pi/extensions/` adapters do.
53: 
54: | Hermes hook | Repo guard core | Effect |
55: |---|---|---|
56: | `pre_llm_call` | skill advisor CLI; spec-gate classifier | Appends the advisor brief every turn and classifies the prompt for the Gate 3 spec-folder gate; the question itself is delivered at the first mutation, not on the turn; the classification is skipped for an orchestrated leaf |
57: | `pre_tool_call` | self-dispatch refusal; read-only refusal; spec-gate enforcement; dispatch preflight lint; task-dispatch guard; MCP route guard; sk-git advisory | Refuses a nested `hermes chat`; refuses the write and command tools when `SPECKIT_HERMES_READ_ONLY=1`; blocks a `write_file` or `patch` the enforced spec gate has not been bound for yet; blocks a `cli-*` dispatch or a `delegate_task` the guards reject; stages the sk-git and MCP-route advisories |
58: | `transform_tool_result` | the Gate 3 notice for an un-enforced write; the staged advisories; post-edit quality | Appends the Gate 3 notice to the first write of an open-gate session, the staged advisories, and the post-edit quality warning for `write_file` and `patch` (the core runs here because post and transform hooks run on separate bounded threads) |
59: | `on_session_start` | shared goal core | Binds the packet named by `HERMES_SPEC_FOLDER` to the session id |
60: | `pre_verify` | completion-evidence stop | Returns a continue nudge when a completion claim names no evidence |
61: | system prompt sections | session-start context; persona; goal core; session-start guards | Four sections under the 4000-character cap: context, `agent-<name>` persona binding, the core's goal (else the packet slice), and the worktree, dist-freshness, git-hooks and primary-reconcile warnings |
62: | `on_session_end` | session-stop context; session cleanup | Records the closing state and reaps the MCP helpers the process spawned |
63: 
64: Validation: `hermes plugins validate ./.hermes/plugins/repo-guards` and `hermes plugins doctor`. Agent Plugins v1 portable packages exist in Hermes but are deferred here; their hook surface is unsettled.
65: 
66: ---
67: 
68: ## 4. WHAT A DISPATCH ASSUMES
69: 
70: The project plugin `repo-guards` (`.hermes/plugins/repo-guards/`) carries the repo guards into a Hermes session when `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS=1` is set and `repo-guards` is listed under `plugins.enabled`; without both, a Hermes dispatch runs with no repo guard hooks. The prompt's preamble and the runtime's dispatch stack are the guards. The packet's hard rule `hooks-user-level` states the boundary so nobody claims otherwise.

30: 
31: ---
32: 
33: ## 2. SHELL HOOKS (USER-LEVEL)
34: 
35: Shell-script hooks:
36: 
37: - **Declared:** under `hooks:` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`.
38: - **Gated:** by a per-command consent allowlist at `~/.hermes/shell-hooks-allowlist.json`.
39: - **Inspected:** with `hermes hooks list|test|doctor`.
40: - **Bypassed:** on a headless run by `--accept-hooks` or `HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS=1`; `hermes -z` sets it automatically.
41: 
42: The repo cannot declare these. None is configured on this machine (observed 2026-09-14: `hooks:` absent, `~/.hermes/hooks/` empty). A dispatch never passes `--accept-hooks` unless the operator declared hooks and asked for it.
43: 
44: ---
45: 
46: ## 3. PROJECT PLUGIN (REPO-CARRIABLE)
47: 
48: Native plugins load from `./.hermes/plugins/<name>/` when `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS` is set, and their hook list covers every guard core this repo runs (source-read: `hermes_cli/plugins.py`). The plugin at `.hermes/plugins/repo-guards/` re-implements nothing:
49: 
50: - Each hook shells out to the existing `.mjs` or `.sh` core under `.skilled/hooks/`.
51: - It maps the core's result to Hermes's block-or-continue contract.
52: - It fails open on a core error, as the `.pi/extensions/` adapters do.
53: 
54: | Hermes hook | Repo guard core | Effect |
55: |---|---|---|
56: | `pre_llm_call` | skill advisor CLI; spec-gate classifier | Appends the advisor brief every turn and classifies the prompt for the Gate 3 spec-folder gate; the question itself is delivered at the first mutation, not on the turn; the classification is skipped for an orchestrated leaf |
57: | `pre_tool_call` | self-dispatch refusal; read-only refusal; spec-gate enforcement; dispatch preflight lint; task-dispatch guard; MCP route guard; sk-git advisory | Refuses a nested `hermes chat`; refuses the write and command tools when `SPECKIT_HERMES_READ_ONLY=1`; blocks a `write_file` or `patch` the enforced spec gate has not been bound for yet; blocks a `cli-*` dispatch or a `delegate_task` the guards reject; stages the sk-git and MCP-route advisories |
58: | `transform_tool_result` | the Gate 3 notice for an un-enforced write; the staged advisories; post-edit quality | Appends the Gate 3 notice to the first write of an open-gate session, the staged advisories, and the post-edit quality warning for `write_file` and `patch` (the core runs here because post and transform hooks run on separate bounded threads) |
59: | `on_session_start` | shared goal core | Binds the packet named by `HERMES_SPEC_FOLDER` to the session id |
60: | `pre_verify` | completion-evidence stop | Returns a continue nudge when a completion claim names no evidence |
61: | system prompt sections | session-start context; persona; goal core; session-start guards | Four sections under the 4000-character cap: context, `agent-<name>` persona binding, the core's goal (else the packet slice), and the worktree, dist-freshness, git-hooks and primary-reconcile warnings |
62: | `on_session_end` | session-stop context; session cleanup | Records the closing state and reaps the MCP helpers the process spawned |
63: 
64: Validation: `hermes plugins validate ./.hermes/plugins/repo-guards` and `hermes plugins doctor`. Agent Plugins v1 portable packages exist in Hermes but are deferred here; their hook surface is unsettled.
65: 
66: ---
67: 
68: ## 4. WHAT A DISPATCH ASSUMES
69: 
70: The project plugin `repo-guards` (`.hermes/plugins/repo-guards/`) carries the repo guards into a Hermes session when `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS=1` is set and `repo-guards` is listed under `plugins.enabled`; without both, a Hermes dispatch runs with no repo guard hooks. The prompt's preamble and the runtime's dispatch stack are the guards. The packet's hard rule `hooks-user-level` states the boundary so nobody claims otherwise.

15: # Hermes CLI Unique Capabilities
16: 
17: Reference for the Hermes surfaces that differ from `cli-codex`, `cli-claude-code`, `cli-opencode`, `cli-cursor`, `cli-devin` and `cli-pi`. Everything here is source-read on v0.21.1 unless marked observed; the contract pin records the live checks.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: ### Purpose
24: 
25: Give a dispatcher the Hermes surfaces that behave unlike every sibling, so it knows what a leaf may rely on and what stays an operator step.
26: 
27: ### When to Use
28: 
29: - Choosing the `-t` toolset list for a leaf
30: - Checking whether a project skill or plugin will load
31: - Planning a write that lands inside `.hermes/`
32: - Deciding whether MCP, hooks or profiles can ship in the repo
33: 
34: ### Core Principle
35: 
36: Hermes exposes more of its surface through named toolsets and user-level configuration than any sibling, and it reads a repo's `.hermes/` folder for exactly two things: skills and plugins. Knowing which is which decides what a dispatch may rely on and what stays an operator step.
37: 
38: ---
39: 
40: ## 2. TOOLSETS
41: 
42: `-t LIST` replaces the configured toolset roster for the run. Toolsets relevant to dispatch (from `toolsets.py`):
43: 
44: | Toolset | Carries | Leaf policy |
45: |---|---|---|
46: | `terminal` | Shell execution | Included for write leaves |
47: | `file` | `read_file`, `write_file`, `patch`, `search_files` | Always: it is the only toolset that reads files. A read-only leaf keeps it without `terminal`, and the repo plugin refuses the write tools under `SPECKIT_HERMES_READ_ONLY=1` |
48: | `search` | `web_search` only (no file search) | Never as a stand-in for file reading; `web` covers it when web search is allowed |
49: | `skills` | Skill loading and management | Included for write leaves |
50: | `todo` | Task list | Always |
51: | `web` | `web_search`, `web_extract` | Per the web-search policy: `live` and `inherit` include it, `disabled` omits it |
52: | `<mcp server name>` | Every enabled tool of that server | Named explicitly (for example `code_mode`) or the server is invisible to the run (observed 2026-09-14) |
53: | `delegation` | `delegate_task` sub-agents | **Never** for a leaf: it spawns agents outside the runner's boundary |
54: | `memory` | Memory read and write | **Never** for a leaf: it bleeds state across sessions |
55: | `clarify` | Asks the user a question | **Never** headless: nobody answers |
56: | `browser`, `vision`, `code_execution`, `computer_use` | Heavier surfaces | Off unless the task names them |
57: 
58: Hermes's stock roster enables `delegation` and `memory`, which is why every dispatch passes an explicit list.
59: 
60: ---
61: 
62: ## 3. REPO-LOCAL SKILLS
63: 
64: Hermes loads project skills from `./.hermes/skills` and `./.agents/skills`, resolved from the nearest project root, but only after `hermes skills trust` has recorded the root in `skills.trusted_project_dirs` of the **user-level** config. The repo cannot carry the grant.
65: 
66: - Every project skill directory is **scanned in full at session start** by Hermes's static scanner, and a symlinked directory is walked like a real one: observed 2026-09-14, the whole-tree link ran the scanner for over ten minutes and quarantined every hub, and a single linked skill directory (`cli-hermes`) was quarantined on 37 findings from its references and scripts.
67: - The repo therefore ships `.hermes/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` as generated markdown-only copies of all 56 canonical `SKILL.md` files plus `agent-<name>` copies of the 12 shared agents (`sync-skills-hermes.cjs`), each naming its canonical source; a session starts in about 17 seconds and `-s <name>` preloads any of them (verified live for `sk-git`, `cli-hermes` and `system-spec-kit`).
68: - `hermes skills list` enumerates the loadable copies as `local` rows, 61 of the 68 on 2026-09-15; the earlier "no project rows" reading was an artifact of the symlink design, under which every skill was quarantined and therefore excluded from the index.
69: - All 174 files pass Hermes's hard validator (name, description, body, name matches directory). Every description exceeds the 60-character listing budget and is truncated with an ellipsis; loading is unaffected, routing signal is.
70: - Never use per-file symlinks either: the scanner flags a symlink resolving outside a skill directory as a critical traversal, and quarantine is per skill directory and fail-closed. Six of the copies (`cli-cursor`, `cli-devin`, `cli-opencode`, `deep-research`, `mcp-aside-devtools`, `sk-create-repo-rule`) are quarantined on prose patterns in their own text. A quarantine is total: the skill leaves the index, the listing and `skill_view`, and `-s <name>` fails with `Unknown skill(s): <name>` and exit 1 (observed 2026-09-15 on `cli-opencode`). Hermes has no configuration knob for it, so a quarantined skill reaches a dispatch only by having its text named in the prompt.
71: - `hermes skills list` reports the load result: a `local` row means the copy loaded, its absence means the scanner quarantined it. A live session with `-s <name>` quoting the skill remains the stronger proof, because the listing does not show what reached the model.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: ## 4. PROJECT PLUGINS
76: 
77: Native plugins load from `~/.hermes/plugins/<name>/` and, opt-in through `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS`, from `./.hermes/plugins/<name>/`, but only when the plugin's key is also listed under `plugins.enabled` in the user-level config; `hermes plugins enable` refuses a project key, so that line is added by hand (observed 2026-09-14). The plugin hook list covers `pre_tool_call`, `pre_verify`, `on_session_start`, `on_session_end`, `subagent_start`, `subagent_stop`, `pre_gateway_dispatch` and more (source-read: `hermes_cli/plugins.py`). This is the repo-carriable vehicle for the guard cores; see [hook-contract.md](./hook-contract.md).
78: 
79: ---
80: 
81: ## 5. THE `.hermes/` WRITE GUARD
82: 
83: Hermes's file tools treat any write whose immediate parent directory is `.hermes` as a protected-instruction write that requires approval (source-read: `tools/file_tools_write_guards.py`). A dispatched leaf therefore cannot author the repo's `.hermes/` files without `--yolo`, and those files are authored from outside Hermes.
84: 
85: ---
86: 
87: ## 6. PROFILES AND HOME
88: 
89: `--profile NAME` (or `-p`) sets `HERMES_HOME` before any module import, scoping config, `.env`, `auth.json`, sessions, memories, skills and logs to that home. Profiles are independent islands: a fresh one holds no credentials. The fan-out never sets a profile; shared home plus `--ignore-rules` is the posture until a seeded-credential contract exists.
90: 
91: ---
92: 
93: ## 7. SUBSYSTEMS THAT STAY OFF
94: 
95: The curator, gateway, cron, kanban, voice and desktop subsystems are off by default and `chat` spawns none of them. `hermes pause` stops cron, kanban and gateway turns only, not a CLI dispatch. Telemetry is opt-in. Startup for `hermes --version` measured 0.86 seconds on this machine, a lower bound for a real dispatch.
96: 
97: ---
98: 
99: ## 8. WHAT HERMES CANNOT CARRY IN THE REPO
100: 
101: Config (`config.yaml`), shell hooks and their consent allowlist, MCP servers (`mcp_servers:`), the provider block and the trust grant. Each is an operator step this skill documents; a dispatch never performs one.

14: # Hermes CLI Integration Patterns
15: 
16: How the calling AI integrates Hermes without duplicating the deep-loop executor. The shared runtime owns process construction; this reference never inserts a packet-local shell wrapper between the skill and that runtime.
17: 
18: ## 1. OVERVIEW
19: 
20: ### Purpose
21: 
22: The calling AI is the conductor; Hermes is the delegated executor.
23: 
24: ### When to Use
25: 
26: - Dispatching a write task to Hermes.
27: - Running a read-only review through Hermes.
28: - Cross-validating a finding against a sibling runtime.
29: - Fanning out a research or review lineage.
30: - Continuing a Hermes session.
31: 
32: ### Core Principle
33: 
34: Every pattern below ends with the conductor reading the exit code, stdout and stderr and verifying the result with the command the prompt named.
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. PATTERNS
39: 
40: ### Write dispatch
41: 
42: 1. Probe `command -v hermes` and `hermes config get providers.llmgateway.base_url`.
43: 2. Write the prompt file: preamble, inlined persona, task, exact files, acceptance, verification command.
44: 3. Dispatch with `--yolo`, `--ignore-rules`, `--source tool`, the leaf toolset list, `--run-budget` under your timeout.
45: 4. Read exit code; on 0 read stdout and run the verification command yourself.
46: 5. Diff the paths touched against the paths authorized; anything else goes back out.
47: 
48: ### Read-only review
49: 
50: Same shape without `--yolo`, with `-t file,todo` and `SPECKIT_HERMES_READ_ONLY=1` in the environment so the repo plugin refuses the write tools (the fan-out sets both for a read-only lineage). The prompt asks for findings with `file:line` citations and forbids edits. Open every citation you are about to repeat.
51: 
52: ### Cross-validation
53: 
54: Dispatch the same brief to Hermes on `glm-5.3-flash` and to a sibling runtime (Pi on the same gateway model, or Codex). Compare findings; where they disagree, name what would settle it. Agreement between two runs of the same model is not corroboration.
55: 
56: ### Fan-out lineage
57: 
58: Use `--executor=cli-hermes` on `/deep:research` or `/deep:review`.
59: 
60: - **Timeout:** set the lineage `timeoutSeconds` to 900 or more. The one live research iteration ran 1042 seconds against a 600-second setting and finished only because the runner's ceiling is twice `iterations × timeoutSeconds` (observed 2026-09-14).
61: - **MCP servers:** a lineage may also name them in `liveTools.mcpServers`; the builder appends them to `-t`.
62: - **Runtime:** builds the command, passes the prompt on stdin, applies write containment to the lineage directory, and treats exit 1 as failure.
63: - **Ceiling:** keep `iterations × timeoutSeconds` under the four-hour lineage ceiling.
64: 
65: ### Session continuation
66: 
67: Capture `session_id:` from stderr. A follow-up may resume with `hermes chat --resume <id>`, but a dispatch never resumes an operator's interactive session, and the resumed run still passes `--ignore-rules` and an explicit toolset list.
68: 
69: ---
70: 
71: ## 3. ANTI-PATTERNS
72: 
73: | Anti-pattern | Why it fails | Do instead |
74: |---|---|---|
75: | `hermes -z "<prompt>"` for a dispatch | No session id, auto-approves everything, auto-accepts hooks | `chat -Q --oneshot --query-file` |
76: | Omitting `--yolo` on a write task | Ordinary writes still run; a step Hermes flags as dangerous is blocked headless and the leaf reports it | Pass `--yolo` with every write or terminal toolset; never on a read-only run |
77: | Omitting `--ignore-rules` | `SOUL.md`, memories and CWD rules enter the leaf prompt | Always pass it |
78: | Default toolset roster | `delegation` and `memory` are enabled | Explicit `-t` list |
79: | `--worktree` | Writes `.git/worktrees/` inside the repo; containment reverts it | Let the runner own isolation |
80: | Trusting exit 0 alone | A budget-cut partial answer also exits 0 | Verify with the named command |
81: | `hermes import-agent` | Copies repo state into the user home, bypasses trust | Inline personas; use prompt templates |
82: | Relocating `HERMES_HOME` per lineage | A fresh home has no credentials | Shared home plus `--ignore-rules` |
83: 
84: ---
85: 
86: ## 4. HANDBACK
87: 
88: Report three things:
89: 
90: - What ran and what it returned (exit code, stdout head, `session_id:`).
91: - What the verification command showed.
92: - Which paths changed.
93: 
94: A Hermes `COMPLETE` in stdout is a claim about itself until the verification command confirms it.

29: - Fanning out a research or review lineage.
30: - Continuing a Hermes session.
31: 
32: ### Core Principle
33: 
34: Every pattern below ends with the conductor reading the exit code, stdout and stderr and verifying the result with the command the prompt named.
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. PATTERNS
39: 
40: ### Write dispatch
41: 
42: 1. Probe `command -v hermes` and `hermes config get providers.llmgateway.base_url`.
43: 2. Write the prompt file: preamble, inlined persona, task, exact files, acceptance, verification command.
44: 3. Dispatch with `--yolo`, `--ignore-rules`, `--source tool`, the leaf toolset list, `--run-budget` under your timeout.
45: 4. Read exit code; on 0 read stdout and run the verification command yourself.
46: 5. Diff the paths touched against the paths authorized; anything else goes back out.
47: 
48: ### Read-only review
49: 
50: Same shape without `--yolo`, with `-t file,todo` and `SPECKIT_HERMES_READ_ONLY=1` in the environment so the repo plugin refuses the write tools (the fan-out sets both for a read-only lineage). The prompt asks for findings with `file:line` citations and forbids edits. Open every citation you are about to repeat.
51: 
52: ### Cross-validation
53: 
54: Dispatch the same brief to Hermes on `glm-5.3-flash` and to a sibling runtime (Pi on the same gateway model, or Codex). Compare findings; where they disagree, name what would settle it. Agreement between two runs of the same model is not corroboration.
55: 
56: ### Fan-out lineage
57: 
58: Use `--executor=cli-hermes` on `/deep:research` or `/deep:review`.
59: 
60: - **Timeout:** set the lineage `timeoutSeconds` to 900 or more. The one live research iteration ran 1042 seconds against a 600-second setting and finished only because the runner's ceiling is twice `iterations × timeoutSeconds` (observed 2026-09-14).
61: - **MCP servers:** a lineage may also name them in `liveTools.mcpServers`; the builder appends them to `-t`.
62: - **Runtime:** builds the command, passes the prompt on stdin, applies write containment to the lineage directory, and treats exit 1 as failure.
63: - **Ceiling:** keep `iterations × timeoutSeconds` under the four-hour lineage ceiling.
64: 
65: ### Session continuation
66: 
67: Capture `session_id:` from stderr. A follow-up may resume with `hermes chat --resume <id>`, but a dispatch never resumes an operator's interactive session, and the resumed run still passes `--ignore-rules` and an explicit toolset list.
68: 
69: ---
70: 
71: ## 3. ANTI-PATTERNS
72:

74: |---|---|---|

76: | Omitting `--yolo` on a write task | Ordinary writes still run; a step Hermes flags as dangerous is blocked headless and the leaf reports it | Pass `--yolo` with every write or terminal toolset; never on a read-only run |
77: | Omitting `--ignore-rules` | `SOUL.md`, memories and CWD rules enter the leaf prompt | Always pass it |
78: | Default toolset roster | `delegation` and `memory` are enabled | Explicit `-t` list |
79: | `--worktree` | Writes `.git/worktrees/` inside the repo; containment reverts it | Let the runner own isolation |
80: | Trusting exit 0 alone | A budget-cut partial answer also exits 0 | Verify with the named command |
81: | `hermes import-agent` | Copies repo state into the user home, bypasses trust | Inline personas; use prompt templates |
82: | Relocating `HERMES_HOME` per lineage | A fresh home has no credentials | Shared home plus `--ignore-rules` |
83: 
84: ---
85: 
86: ## 4. HANDBACK
87: 
88: Report three things:
89: 
90: - What ran and what it returned (exit code, stdout head, `session_id:`).
91: - What the verification command showed.
92: - Which paths changed.
93: 
94: A Hermes `COMPLETE` in stdout is a claim about itself until the verification command confirms it.

22: 
23: ### Purpose

28:

32: 
33: ### Core Principle
34: 
35: The roster is closed at five ids so generic provider routing cannot broaden dispatch, and the provider is the one whose credential the operator already holds for the other runtimes.
36: 
37: ---
38: 
39: ## 2. THE PROVIDER CONTRACT
40: 
41: Hermes resolves `--provider NAME` against its built-in providers or a user-defined block under `providers:` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`. The LLM Gateway (DevPass) is not a built-in, so the operator declares it. 44: providers:
45:   llmgateway:
46:     base_url: https://api.llmgateway.io/v1
47:     key_env: LLMGATEWAY_API_KEY
48: ```
49: 
50: The key itself lives in `~/.hermes/.env` or the shell; it never appears in a prompt, a repo file, or this skill's files. This is an operator step: no dispatch, plugin or repo file writes it. The field names were confirmed live on 2026-09-14 (`hermes config set providers.llmgateway.base_url ...` and `.key_env`); the shape above follows Hermes's `custom` provider convention (source-read: `cli-config.yaml.example`, `hermes_cli/config_providers.py`).
51: 
52: Other credential kinds on this machine do not transfer: Hermes keeps its own OAuth sessions in `~/.hermes/auth.json`, and its Codex import reads `~/.codex/auth.json` once at login rather than sharing it. A Codex OAuth import is a possible second provider later; it is not on this roster.
53: 
54: ---
55:

57: 
58: | Model id | Provider | Reasoning | Standing | Notes |
59: |---|---|---|---|---|
60: | `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` | `llmgateway` | pinned `max` | **observed 2026-10-22**: a live fan-out dispatch with no model pinned built `--model deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` and replied `OK` | The rotation default; the same literal cli-pi dispatches through DevPass |
61: | `deepseek-v4.1-flash` | `llmgateway` | pinned `max` | **observed 2026-09-14**: smoke exit 0, fan-out lineage dispatched | The 2026-09-10 release, still selectable and pinnable; llmgateway's DeepSeek provider route for it is Deactivating on Oct 24, 2026, so a pinned run must move to the `-1017` id before then |
62: | `glm-5.3-flash` | `llmgateway` | pinned `max` | **observed 2026-09-14**: smoke exit 0 at `max` and `none` | The second lens; flat-price on DevPass |
63: | `minimax-m3` | `llmgateway` | the caller's effort | probed live on this route, per `SKILL.md` | In `HERMES_SUPPORTED_MODELS` and its fan-out mirror |
64: | `qwen3.8-max` | `llmgateway` | the caller's effort | probed live on this route, per `SKILL.md` | In `HERMES_SUPPORTED_MODELS` and its fan-out mirror |

73:

82: | `glm-5.3-flash` | `none` | exit 0, `OK`, 17 s |
83: | `deepseek-v4.1-flash` | `low` | exit 0, `OK`, 21 s |
84: | `deepseek-v4.1-flash` | `ultra` | exit 0, `OK`, 24 s |
85:

95:   -t terminal,file,skills,todo,web --yolo --in "$PWD" </dev/null
96: ```

103:

45: 
46: ### Persona goes in the prompt body
47:

A persona-less leaf runs as a generic assistant and drops its tool scope, verification gates and output contract.
49: 
50: ### The prompt travels on stdin or in a file
51: 
52: Use `--query-file <path>` for any prompt longer than a sentence, or `--query-file -` to feed stdin. Hermes reads the file verbatim: quotes, `$(...)` and backticks survive. Argv `-q` is for one-line asks only and risks the argv length limit on an iteration brief.
53: 
54: ### Say what the leaf may touch
55: 
56: Hermes has no OS sandbox. The prompt states the write surface explicitly (the lineage directory, or the named files). 61:

63: 
64: A dispatched leaf must not run `hermes skills trust`, `hermes mcp add`, `hermes config set`, `hermes plugins install` or `hermes import-agent`. Those are operator steps; a prompt that needs one stops and reports instead.

73: - [ ] Model is one of the five roster ids in `HERMES_SUPPORTED_MODELS`. Provider is `llmgateway`.
74: - [ ] `--run-budget` under the caller's timeout; stdin fed by `--query-file -` or closed.

49:   --reasoning max --ignore-rules --source tool --max-turns 200 --run-budget 840 \
50:   -t terminal,file,skills,todo,web --yolo --in "$PWD" </dev/null
51: ```

61:   --reasoning max --ignore-rules --source tool --max-turns 60 --run-budget 300 \
62:   -t file,todo --in "$PWD" </dev/null
63: ```
64:

76:

81:   --executor=cli-hermes --model=deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --label=hermes --iters=5 \
82:   --stop-policy=max-iterations
83: ```

89: - `--max-turns 200`
90: - `--run-budget` one margin under the lineage timeout
91: - `-t terminal,file,skills,todo`, plus `web` per the web-search policy
92: - `--reasoning max`, the roster's pinned tier
93: 
94: `--worktree` and `-z` never appear.

99: 
100: Run the same review prompt through Hermes and through a sibling runtime, then compare findings rather than averaging them:
101: 
102: ```bash

104: pi -p --offline --model llmgateway/glm-5.3-flash --thinking max "$(cat /tmp/review.md)" </dev/null > pi.out
105: ```
106: 
107: Disagreements name what would settle them; a tally is not a finding.

# Pi CLI Prompt Templates

Copy-ready templates for common Pi CLI dispatch shapes. Replace `[placeholders]` with your values. Apply the canonical prompt-quality card before using them.

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

This asset provides structured, copy-paste ready dispatch templates for invoking Pi CLI across its print, JSON, and RPC surfaces. Each template includes the full command with flags plus a concrete example.

### Usage

1. Find the template matching your task's dispatch shape.
2. Copy the command.
3. Replace `[placeholders]` with actual values.
4. Run through the shared deep-loop runtime, not a packet-local wrapper.

### Flag Reference

> **Exit code caveat:** the pin observed exit `0` then exit `1` on identical unauthenticated calls. Every template below assumes the caller inspects output text, not the exit code alone.
> **Offline caveat:** `--verbose` without `--offline` can hang 2+ minutes when no network path is available. Pass `--offline` whenever no live provider call is intended.
> **No enforced model allowlist at this layer:** unlike `cli-cursor`/`cli-devin`, Pi is a multi-provider passthrough. Use the authenticated provider roster in `cli-reference.md` §13 rather than guessing at an unconfirmed model id.

| Flag | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `-p` / `--print` | Non-interactive mode. Process the prompt and exit. Skill default for one-shot dispatch. |
| `--mode text` | Text output, the default mode. |
| `--mode json` | JSONL event stream, one JSON object per line, not a single document. |
| `--mode rpc` | Persistent stdin/stdout JSONL protocol. Requires a lifecycle owner (see `integration-patterns.md` §7). |
| `--tools <list>` | Comma-separated tool allowlist (e.g. `read,grep,find,ls`), enforced by the CLI, not a prompt sentence. |
| `--thinking <level>` | `off` through `max`, independent of `--model`, unlike Cursor/Devin's model-id-baked effort tiers. |

+-- SKILL.md                    # Hard rules, dispatch shape, gotchas

| `references/agent-delegation.md` | Persona inlining, persona skills, `delegate_task`, command templates |
| `references/hook-contract.md` | Shell hooks versus the project plugin, the guard-core hook map |
| `references/mcp-policy.md` | Operator steps for MCP and deny-by-default per tool |
| `assets/prompt-quality-card.md` | Thin delegator to the canonical prompt-models card |
| `assets/prompt-templates.md` | Write, read-only, generation and fan-out scaffolds |
| `feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md` | Canonical current-state inventory for the shipped surface |
| `feature-catalog/dispatch-guards/` | Hard-rule preflight checks and dispatch-shape recognition |
| `feature-catalog/fanout-dispatch/` | Executor kind, closed roster, run budget and toolset policy |
| `feature-catalog/hub-registration/` | Hub mode registration |
| `feature-catalog/prompt-contract/` | Prompt card and improver eligibility |
| `feature-catalog/runtime-surface/` | The `.hermes/` runtime folder and the repo-guards plugin |

The repo-root `.hermes/` folder is the runtime surface Hermes itself reads.

| Path | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `.hermes/skills/<name>/` | One generated markdown-only `SKILL.md` per canonical skill, all 56, naming its canonical directory. Never a symlink: Hermes's static scanner walks everything it reaches, costs ten minutes per session start and quarantines every hub |
| `.hermes/plugins/repo-guards/` | The hand-authored project plugin bridging the repo's guard cores into Hermes hooks |
| `.hermes/prompts/*.md` | Generated pointer stubs, one per `.skilled/commands/**` file, named by the flattened command path |
| `.hermes/SYNC.md` | The sync manifest: what derives from `.skilled`, what can drift and how to regenerate it |

There is no `.hermes/agents/`, because Hermes has no flag that loads an agent file.

## 6. CONFIGURATION

Four steps are the operator's and live in the user-level `~/.hermes/`. No repo file performs them and no dispatch should claim otherwise.

| Step | Command or setting | Why it is user-level |
|---|---|---|
| Provider | A `providers:` block named `llmgateway` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` with `key_env: LLMGATEWAY_API_KEY` | Hermes reads provider config only from the user home |
| Skill trust | `hermes skills trust`, run once from the repo root | The trust grant is recorded per project in the user config |
| Project plugins | `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS=1` in the session environment, plus `repo-guards` under `plugins.enabled` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` | `hermes plugins enable` refuses project keys, so the line is added by hand |

# cli-codex

> Get OpenAI-grade coding work into any AI runtime: sandboxed file edits, live web research, diff-aware reviews and a second opinion on your code, all delivered through the `codex` CLI without leaving your current session.

---

## 1. AT A GLANCE

| Aspect | What you get |
|---|---|
| **Use it for** | Sandboxed coding, repo analysis, PR review, live web research and cross-model validation through OpenAI's `codex` CLI |
| **Invoke with** | "codex", "openai", "web search", "second opinion" or auto-routing on Codex keywords |
| **Works on** | Any external runtime (Claude Code, Copilot, raw shell) that needs to reach the `codex` binary |
| **Produces** | Code edits in a sandbox, text responses, diff-aware reviews and web-enriched research |

---

## 2. OVERVIEW

### Why This Skill Exists

A non-Codex assistant has no built-in way to reach the `codex` binary. When a task wants OpenAI-model strengths, like sandboxed file edits, live web browsing mid-execution, the diff-aware review workflow or a second model's opinion, the caller either hand-builds fragile `codex exec` invocations and picks flags by trial or skips the capability. The worst trap: `codex exec` defaults to a read-only sandbox, so edit tasks fail silently. Auth handling, service-tier selection, sandbox mapping and reasoning effort all become guesswork. If the calling assistant is itself Codex, a circular self-dispatch burns tokens for no value. This skill standardizes the dispatch, the auth pre-flight, the self-invocation guard and the readiness check. The caller never builds its own CLI wrapper.

### What It Does

cli-codex is the single routing point for external runtimes that need Codex CLI. A smart router scores the task against intent signals (code generation, review, web research, architecture exploration, agent delegation) and loads only the references that match. It fails closed when `command -v codex` cannot resolve the binary. A three-layer self-invocation guard refuses to load if the caller is already inside Codex. Orchestrated execution delegates to the shipped deep-loop runtime. This packet does not build a second adapter.

It does not write application code or manage spec folders. `sk-code` owns code standards and tests. `system-spec-kit` owns spec folders, memory and continuity. cli-codex dispatches to Codex and hands the result back to the caller.

### The Dispatch Capabilities

# cli-cursor

> Cursor's own model can run the work while you stay in your current assistant. This skill makes that handoff safe and repeatable: sandboxed coding, Composer-model dispatch, read-only plan passes and read-only ask passes, all without leaving your runtime.

---

## 1. AT A GLANCE

| Aspect | What you get |
|---|---|
| **Use it for** | Sandboxed coding, Composer-model dispatch, read-only plan or ask exploration and cross-model validation through Cursor's `cursor-agent` CLI |
| **Invoke with** | "cursor", "cursor agent", "composer", "second opinion" or auto-routing on Cursor keywords |
| **Works on** | Any external runtime (Claude Code, Codex, raw shell) that needs to reach the `cursor-agent` binary |
| **Produces** | Code edits in a workspace, text responses and read-only plan or ask analyses |

---

## 2. OVERVIEW

### Why This Skill Exists

A non-Cursor assistant has no built-in way to reach the `cursor-agent` binary. When a task wants Cursor's own Composer model, a read-only plan or ask pass or a second AI opinion, the caller either hand-builds fragile `cursor-agent -p` invocations and picks flags by trial or skips the capability.

Two traps make naive dispatch dangerous:

- **The zero exit code.** `cursor-agent -p` exits `0` even when the account is not authenticated, so an exit-code check reports success on a dispatch that never reached a model.
- **The shared config surface.** The CLI also shares its config surface with the Cursor editor, so a dispatched session silently inherits editor-level hooks, MCP servers, rules and other configuration.

If the calling assistant is itself running inside Cursor CLI, a circular self-dispatch burns tokens for no value.

This skill standardizes the dispatch, runs a text-based auth pre-flight and guards against self-invocation so the caller never builds its own wrapper.
